meta.title: The new complete semicolon feature fails with closures
meta.fix_ref: rust-lang/rust-analyzer#18132 (fix: Don't complete `;` when in closure return expression)
meta.build_notes: GitHub release assets rust-analyzer-aarch64-apple-darwin.gz of the weekly tags 2024-09-16 and 2024-09-30; git tag --contains puts the fix first in 2024-09-23, whose release lacks the macOS arm64 asset, so the next release is the post build. The sysroot is the local rustup toolchain (rustc 1.98.1).
meta.notes: The then-new completion of ';' after unit-returning functions also fired for the expression body of a closure, which is commonly not a block; 'baz(|| foo(););' does not parse. The window is widened to 2024-09-30 because git tag --contains puts the fix first in 2024-09-23, whose release lacks the macOS arm64 asset (candidate mapping).

settings_note: The issue names no settings; the session keeps checkOnSave off (native analysis only).

files.note: the fix's regression test no_semicolon_in_closure_ret (crates/ide-completion/src/render/function.rs at 00037c18), cursor marker $0 removed; the issue (filed by the fix's author as a note to self) describes the case in words only
a library crate around the snippet (package name, version, edition 2021)

repro.steps: Open src/lib.rs. Request completion after 'fo' in 'baz(|| fo);' (line 3, character 13) and accept foo. Reported (issue text): completing a unit-returning function as the expression body of a closure appends ';', which breaks the code. Probe: the edited text must have no parse error that the original did not have.
